brief: Investor sentiment and hedge fund positioning are broadly depressed, per a Market Ear round-up of bank data. Deutsche Bank shows the AAII bull-minus-bear sentiment spread near the bottom of its long-run range. Morgan Stanley's Global Risk Demand Index has moved into its "fear" zone. JPM data put equity long/short net leverage around the 19th percentile on a 12-month basis. Goldman Prime shows fundamental long/short gross leverage at the 33rd percentile and net leverage at just the 7th percentile over the past year. A Deutsche Bank-sourced chart of JPMorgan's Tactical Positioning Monitor points to further de-risking over the past week, nearing July lows. Credit fund flows have recently turned negative amid rates uncertainty, per BofA/EPFR data. A JPM-sourced chart of Deutsche Bank's consolidated equity positioning indicator sits at the 48th percentile, essentially the middle of its historical range, labeled a "high conviction neutral" read. The note draws no forward call. It reports where each gauge currently stands.
